title: Secure monitoring: SNMPv3 and NetFlow
domain: Secure Network Access, Visibility, and Enforcement
blurb: Replace community strings with authenticated, encrypted SNMPv3 and export flows to Secure Network Analytics.
purpose: You can't defend what you can't see, but monitoring itself must be secure. This lab replaces SNMP community strings with authenticated, encrypted SNMPv3 and exports Flexible NetFlow to an analytics collector. It covers secure telemetry and visibility.
scenario: R1 is still polled with SNMPv2c and the community string **public**, and the security team can't see who is talking to whom. Move monitoring to **SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy** for the NMS at **10.10.99.20**, and export Flexible NetFlow from the LAN interface **GigabitEthernet0/1** to the Secure Network Analytics (Stealthwatch) Flow Collector at **10.10.99.30**, UDP **2055**.
topology:
LAN ── Gi0/1 R1 ── Internet
          │
   NMS 10.10.99.20 (SNMPv3)   Flow Collector 10.10.99.30 (NetFlow v9)
objectives: Choose the right SNMPv3 security level
Create the SNMPv3 group, user and trap host
Build a flow record, exporter and monitor
Apply the monitor and see what the collector does with flows

steps.title: Pick the security level
steps.learn: SNMPv3 replaces community strings with users, and it has three security levels. **noAuthNoPriv** is a username only. **authNoPriv** adds a hash to prove the sender (SHA). **authPriv** also encrypts the payload (AES).
steps.task: Match each SNMPv3 level to what it protects.

steps.title: Configure SNMPv3
steps.learn: The **group** sets the security level. The **user** belongs to the group and holds the auth and priv keys. The **host** command sends traps to the NMS as that user. Remove the old community with `no snmp-server community public`.
steps.task: Remove community **public**. Create group **NMS-GROUP** at v3 **priv**. Create user **nmsuser** in it with **sha** auth key **AuthPass123** and **aes 128** priv key **PrivPass123**. Send v3 **priv** traps to **10.10.99.20** as nmsuser.
steps.hint: `no snmp-server community public`, `snmp-server group NMS-GROUP v3 priv`, `snmp-server user nmsuser NMS-GROUP v3 auth sha AuthPass123 priv aes 128 PrivPass123`, `snmp-server host 10.10.99.20 version 3 priv nmsuser`.

commands.note: The plain-text v2c community is gone.
commands.explain: Removes the old public community string, which works like a password sent in clear text.
Creates SNMPv3 group NMS-GROUP with priv, which requires both authentication and encryption.

commands.cmd: snmp-server user nmsuser NMS-GROUP v3 auth sha AuthPass123 priv aes 128 PrivPass123
commands.note: SNMPv3 users don't appear in the running configuration. Their keys are stored separately.
commands.explain: Creates user nmsuser with SHA authentication and AES-128 encryption.
Sends SNMPv3 notifications to the NMS at 10.10.99.20, encrypted, as nmsuser.

steps.title: Build the flow record and exporter
steps.learn: Flexible NetFlow has three parts. The **record** says which fields make a flow unique (`match`) and what to count (`collect`). The **exporter** says where to send flows. The **monitor** ties them together.
steps.task: Create record **FR-SCOR** matching IPv4 source and destination address, protocol, and transport source and destination port, and collecting byte and packet counters. Create exporter **FE-SNA** sending to **10.10.99.30** over UDP **2055** with NetFlow v9.
steps.hint: `flow record FR-SCOR` then `match ipv4 source address`, `match ipv4 destination address`, `match ipv4 protocol`, `match transport source-port`, `match transport destination-port`, `collect counter bytes`, `collect counter packets`. Then `flow exporter FE-SNA`, `destination 10.10.99.30`, `transport udp 2055`, `export-protocol netflow-v9`.

commands.explain: Creates a flow record, which defines what makes a flow and what to count.
Uses the source IPv4 address as a key field.
Uses the destination IPv4 address as a key field.
Uses the IP protocol as a key field.
Uses the source port as a key field.
Uses the destination port as a key field.
Counts bytes for each flow.
Counts packets for each flow.
Creates a flow exporter, which sends records to a collector.
Sends flow records to the collector at 10.10.99.30.
Uses UDP port 2055, a common NetFlow port.
Uses the NetFlow version 9 format.

steps.title: Monitor the LAN interface
steps.task: Create monitor **FM-SCOR** using record **FR-SCOR** and exporter **FE-SNA**, and apply it **inbound** on **GigabitEthernet0/1**.
steps.hint: `flow monitor FM-SCOR`, `record FR-SCOR`, `exporter FE-SNA`, then `interface GigabitEthernet0/1` and `ip flow monitor FM-SCOR input`.

commands.explain: Creates a flow monitor, which ties a record and an exporter together.
Uses record FR-SCOR.
Uses exporter FE-SNA.
Enters the interface to monitor.

commands.note: Flows entering from the LAN are now exported.
commands.explain: Monitors flows coming in on this interface.

steps.title: What the collector sees
steps.question: How does Secure Network Analytics use these flows to find threats?

options.text: It baselines normal behavior for each host and raises alarms on anomalies, such as a workstation suddenly sending gigabytes to an unknown address or scanning many hosts.
It reads the payload of every packet to match malware signatures.
options.why: NetFlow carries metadata (who, when, how much), not payloads. Signature matching is the job of an IPS such as Snort.

options.text: It blocks the traffic on R1 directly.
options.why: Flow analysis is detection and visibility. Blocking takes integration, for example ISE Rapid Threat Containment.

summary: SNMPv3 at authPriv with a group, user and trap host replacing the v2c community, and Flexible NetFlow with a record, an exporter to the Secure Network Analytics collector, and a monitor on the LAN interface.
